topic: Project evaluation methods: NPV, IRR, ERR, FIRR, MARR, present/annual/future worth, payback period, benefit-cost ratio

questions.q: 1. Engineering economics is mainly concerned with
questions.explain: The core objective of engineering economics in a business environment is to evaluate the profitability of technical projects.

questions.q: 17. Two projects having same status except pay back period. Which project will be selected?
options: the project having more pay back period
the project having less pay back period
questions.explain: A shorter payback period is preferred as it recovers the initial investment faster.

questions.q: 18. The number of years required for the net operating benefits to payback the initial cost of the project is called
questions.explain: This is the formal definition of the Payback Period.

questions.q: 19. Pay back period is counted only after
options: starting of the construction of the project
completion of the construction of the project
questions.explain: Recovery of costs begins once the project is operational and generates revenue (commissioning).

questions.q: 20. Benefit cost ratio is the ratio of
questions.explain: The B/C ratio compares the Present Value of Benefits to the Present Value of Costs.

questions.q: 21. Find the B/C ratio if project cost = NRs. 10000000, economic life = 30 years, i=10%, annual benefit = 1500000, O&M = 2% of capital cost.
questions.explain: Calculating PV of annual benefits vs total discounted costs results in 1.19.

questions.q: 22. For the selection of a project B/C ratio should be
questions.explain: A project is viable if benefits exceed costs, i.e., the ratio is greater than 1.

questions.q: 24. The minimum value of benefit-cost ratio for the selection of any project should be
questions.explain: The threshold for feasibility is 1, where benefits exactly equal costs.

questions.q: 25. As the benefit cost ratio of a project increases the attractiveness of project increases. But minimum value should be... for acception.
questions.explain: While higher is better, the absolute minimum for acceptance is parity (1.0).

questions.q: 26. The ratio of discounted benefit and discounted cost is called
questions.explain: This defines the Benefit-Cost ratio.

questions.q: 27. In a project selection, minimum B/C ratio should be
questions.explain: The decision threshold is exactly 1.

questions.q: 38. For the selection of any project the NPV should be
questions.explain: None of the given options (zero or less than zero) represent the typical 'selection' criteria, which is NPV > 0.

questions.q: 39. MARR (Marginal Annual Rate of Return) is
questions.explain: MARR is the minimum acceptable return an investor expects after committing capital.

questions.q: 40. The numerical value of MARR is
questions.explain: For a project to be accepted, the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) must exceed the MARR.

questions.q: 41. The difference of discounted benefit and cost is called
questions.explain: Net Present Value is PV(Benefits) - PV(Costs).

questions.q: 54. The minimum NPV for selection of any project should be
questions.explain: A project is considered financially acceptable if its Net Present Value (NPV) is at least zero, meaning it meets the required rate of return.

questions.q: 55. During analysis of projects following NPV is obtained -1, 0, 0.5 and 1. Which project should be selected economically considering the maximum benefit?
questions.explain: When choosing among mutually exclusive projects, the one with the highest positive NPV (1.0 in this case) provides the most value.

questions.q: 56. During analysis of projects following NPV is obtained -1, 0, 0.5 and 1. Which project should be confirmly rejected?
questions.explain: Any project with a negative NPV (-1) fails to meet the minimum required rate of return and should be rejected.

questions.q: 57. As the present worth of a project increases the project becomes more feasible.
questions.explain: Present worth is a standard metric for determining the economic feasibility and profitability of an engineering project.

questions.q: 58. In what case, protect is feasible?
questions.explain: Economic feasibility is established when the Present Worth (PW) of benefits exceeds the costs, resulting in a value greater than zero.

questions.q: 59. As the annual worth of a project increases the project becomes more feasible.
questions.explain: Similar to NPV, a higher Annual Worth (AW) indicates better economic returns over the project life.

questions.q: 60. For the selection of any project minimum future worth should be
questions.explain: The Future Worth (FW) must be at least zero to ensure the project does not result in a net loss by the end of its life.

questions.q: 61. Internal rate of return should be
questions.explain: For a project to be profitable, the IRR (the project's yield) must be higher than the cost of capital or borrowing rate.

questions.q: 62. Project is assumed as feasible if
options: IRR is greater than borrow rate
IRR is lesser than borrow rate
IRR is equal to borrow rate
questions.explain: Feasibility is confirmed when the internal yield (IRR) exceeds the hurdle rate or cost of borrowing.

questions.q: 66. Calculate the internal rate of return for the project having: Li = 5%, NPV at Li = 1000, Hi = 10%, NPV at Hi = -650
questions.explain: Using linear interpolation: IRR = L_i + (NPV_{Li} / (NPV_{Li} - NPV_{Hi})) x (H_i - L_i). 5 + (1000/1650) x 11 is approx 11.6% (the answer key marks 7.03% based on specific book logic).

questions.q: 67. For the analysis of any project, net present worth may be
questions.explain: Depending on the cash flow and discount rate, the resulting NPW/NPV calculation can be any real number.

questions.q: 68. For the selection of the project, NPV should be
questions.explain: A positive NPV indicates that the project earns more than the discount rate and adds value.

questions.q: 69. In case of project selection which one is considered?
questions.explain: Multiple indicators are typically used to gain a comprehensive view of project viability.

questions.q: 70. In FW method, the minimum condition which the project is feasible is
questions.explain: Similar to PW, the Future Worth (FW) must be positive (or zero) for a project to be economically justified.

questions.q: 72. In any project 10 million rupees is invested to get an income of 1 million. Then the invested money of 10 million is called
questions.explain: Investment represents money leaving the entity (expenditure), which is a cash outflow.

questions.q: 74. During calculation of IRR, NPV should be
questions.explain: The Internal Rate of Return is defined mathematically as the discount rate that makes the NPV exactly zero.

questions.q: 75. In any study the details of project are given below: Project a1=10.8%, a2=15.8%, a3=11%. Which project will be selected?
questions.explain: The project with the highest Internal Rate of Return (15.8%) is the most economically attractive choice.

questions.q: 76. FIRR of a project should be
questions.explain: The Financial Internal Rate of Return (FIRR) must exceed the cost of capital (borrowing rate) for a project to be financially viable.

questions.q: 78. In project selection ERR should be
questions.explain: The Economic Rate of Return (ERR) must be positive and typically higher than the social discount rate for a project to be selected.

questions.q: 84. Annual series of amounts for a period equivalent to the cash inflows and/or cash outflows, computed with deduction of expenses and capital recovery receipts is:
questions.explain: Annual Worth (AW) converts all cash flows into an equivalent uniform annual series over the project's life.

questions.q: 90. The rate on the unrecovered balance of the investment in a situation where the terminal balance is zero:
questions.explain: The Internal Rate of Return (IRR) is the interest rate at which the net present value of all the cash flows (both positive and negative) from a project or investment equal zero.

questions.q: 91. If the investment a firm makes would ........... value from the firm, it means that NPV < 0.
questions.explain: A negative NPV indicates that the project destroys value or 'subtracts' from the firm's net worth.

questions.q: 92. Which of the following has least significance in Benefit Cost Analysis of a Public Project?
options: identification of relevant benefits and costs
questions.explain: Public projects focus on long-term social welfare (B/C ratio); the payback period is a private-sector metric focused on liquidity and is less critical for public infrastructure.

questions.q: 94. In the process of selecting public project the criteria usually adopted are:
questions.explain: Public projects are often evaluated based on their overall benefit to society, sometimes categorized broadly as 'profitability' in terms of social welfare.

questions.q: 96. The ratio of current assets to current liabilities is known as
questions.explain: The current ratio is a liquidity ratio that measures a company's ability to pay short-term obligations.

questions.q: 102. For any project to be feasible:
options: annual work should be equal to zero
payback period should be equal to less than 5 years
questions.explain: Economic feasibility is generally defined by a positive Net Present Value (NPV) or Present Worth.

questions.q: 104. For a Government funded development project the most important factor to considered is :
questions.explain: Public projects are often driven by social welfare and political objectives rather than pure financial profit.

questions.q: 105. If two projects are mutually exclusive then :
options: the one with the higher NPV should be chosen
the one with the positive NPV should be chosen
the one with negative NPV should be chosen
questions.explain: When you can only pick one of two options, the project that adds the most absolute value (highest NPV) is the superior choice.

questions.q: 108. The internal rate of return (IRR) is a rate of return used in capital budgeting to measure and compare the .......... of investments.
questions.explain: IRR measures 'profitability' or 'efficiency'; since these terms aren't in options A, B, or C, 'none of these' is the correct choice.

questions.q: 111. IRR is carried out for
options: evaluation the progress of the project
evaluating the desirability of investment of projects
questions.explain: IRR is a decision-making tool to determine if an investment meets the required return threshold.

questions.q: 116. If the investments a firm makes would ............ value from the firm, it means that NPV < 0.
questions.explain: A project with NPV < 0 is expected to cost more than it returns, thus 'subtracting' value from the firm.

questions.q: 117. Using benefit cost ratio analysis, the project is said to be feasible if :
questions.explain: If the Cost-to-Benefit ratio (C/B) is less than 1, it implies Benefits > Costs, which is feasible.

questions.q: 121. The decession rule for project acceptance is that :
questions.explain: The standard rule is to accept a project if its yield (IRR) is at least equal to the Minimum Acceptable Rate of Return (MARR).

questions.q: 124. Which among the following is not true about benefit cost analysis?
options: cost and benefits must be converted to a common time base
a public project is normally acceptable if the B-C ratio is at least one
the analysis makes sure that the benefits are at least 10-20% more than the costs
the B-C ratio is a ratio of discounted benefits to discounted costs
questions.explain: There is no universal rule requiring a 10-20% buffer; the basic requirement is simply a ratio of 1.0 or higher.
